prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: It’s wild to me that  doesn’t haven’t a better system by which customers can retrieve lost items. Y’all have all the info already 🤔
Delta: Thank you so much for reaching out to us. I'm sorry to hear that you misplaced and something. We appreciate your feedback. *AMC

Customer: Our incoming flight was behind schedule (we haven’t boarded yet and flight was scheduled to leave in 20 minutes) and we only have a 38 minute layover in MSP. Please advise!!!
Delta: Give me a moment to pull up your information. *TAA

Customer: Suspense = checking the   app once you’re boarded to see if the adjacent seat is still empty #toomuchtravel #sleepambitions
Delta: Hello, Rosalind. Pls follow/DM your confirmation or ticket number to take a look. *AFM https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: you should have just de-boarded us. 2 hours sitting here. DL5686
Delta: Not sure why they did not. The Captain would be communicating that to everyone. *TMT

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: delay_cancellation):
"""Any info on DL0479? Says we leave at 8:15 when we haven’t even boarded."""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Hi there! Please DM us your confirmation or ticket number so we can look into DL0479 for you.
